requirement:
The coverage index MUST present a file coverage map of all current first-party
Rust files under {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` as its
primary overview. Its counts MUST use only the records eligible for the
combined view under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, following
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map`.

The overview MUST visibly identify coverage excluded because it is stale,
missing, or unreadable. When those exclusions leave no usable selected
records, the map MUST show coverage as unavailable; when no coverage has been
recorded, files MUST show "not measured" and the collection guidance of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.unavailable` MUST remain visible.
The test and run details required by
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary` MUST remain available on
demand rather than expanded by default.
rationale:
I judged this from the three supplied `{test}` items in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs`. I did not request any implementation source.

**Obligations derived from `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.combined`, and the tests that cover them**

1. **A file map of all current first-party Rust files, using only eligible records.**
   - `file_maps_union_process_locations_and_filter_unexecuted_test_files` checks the combined overview. It asserts "Line coverage: **2/4 (50.0%)**" and per-file cards: `code.rs` shows "2/3 instrumented lines covered" and 66.7%, `zero.rs` shows 0.0%, and `unmeasured.rs` shows "not measured" with no `%`. It also adds a child process to the attempt and expects its locations to be unioned in.
   - `incomplete_attempts_do_not_label_their_files_as_unmeasured_in_a_partial_map` has a good attempt and an unusable attempt. It asserts that `code.rs` is 100.0% from the good attempt only, so the excluded record contributes nothing. The file touched only by the unusable attempt shows "unavailable".
   - `maps_distinguish_no_runs_zero_hits_stale_and_incomplete_coverage` adds a new file `new.rs` after the run. It appears in the map as unavailable, which shows the map covers current files.

2. **Visibly identify coverage excluded as stale, missing, or unreadable.**
   - The partial-map test asserts the index text "1 unavailable test attempts" for a missing profile, and "1 stale test attempts" for a stale selected attempt.
   - `maps_distinguish_no_runs_zero_hits_stale_and_incomplete_coverage` asserts "1 stale test attempts" after the source changes. It asserts "1 unavailable test attempts" after the source is changed back to something different from the captured source. It asserts "Coverage history is incomplete" when `attempt.json` is unreadable.

3. **When exclusions leave no usable selected records, the map shows unavailable.**
   - The stale, unreadable, and corrupt-metadata scenarios in `maps_distinguish_no_runs_zero_hits_stale_and_incomplete_coverage` each assert that the file card contains "unavailable" and no `%`.
   - The per-test failure loop covers no processes, an attempt diagnostic, a process diagnostic, a missing source, and an empty profile. It asserts "**Coverage unavailable:**" with no map and no 0% or "not measured" output.

4. **When no coverage has been recorded, files show "not measured" and the collection guidance stays visible.** The no-runs scenario asserts that `code.rs` shows "not measured" and that the index contains "Run `habeas coverage`".

5. **Test and run details are available on demand, not expanded by default.**
   - The first test renders the index to HTML with pulldown-cmark. It asserts that `<details class="habeas-coverage-details">` is present and not `open`, and that the per-test selector is outside a paragraph.
   - The same test asserts that the detail chapter has no `open` details, contains "Run and attempt details" and "Source lines and individual processes", and places the map before the run details.

**Unresolved gaps:** none. Marking is also present: all three tests carry `{test}` references to `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.combined`. Incompatible-configuration exclusion belongs to the cited `requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`, and the file-discovery rules belong to `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`. This requirement only cites both, so neither is assessed here.

The tests cover each named condition with concrete assertions that would catch violating behavior.

text: :::{req} index.file_map.combined
The coverage index MUST present a file coverage map of all current first-party
Rust files under {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` as its
primary overview. Its counts MUST use only the records eligible for the
combined view under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, following
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map`.
The overview MUST visibly identify coverage excluded because it is stale,
missing, or unreadable. When those exclusions leave no usable selected
records, the map MUST show coverage as unavailable; when no coverage has been
recorded, files MUST show "not measured" and the collection guidance of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.unavailable` MUST remain visible.
The test and run details required by
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary` MUST remain available on
demand rather than expanded by default.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} index.selection
The coverage index MUST combine the most recent recorded test attempt for each
nextest binary and test name among the retained runs. "Most recent" MUST refer
to when the attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer
filtered run MUST update only the tests it executes, leaving other compatible
test records available to the combined view. A newer attempt with missing or
unreadable coverage MUST be shown as unavailable rather than replaced with an
older successful attempt. Results from incompatible instrumented build
configurations MUST NOT be combined under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`.
The main combined view MUST use the instrumented build configuration of the
most recently started recorded test attempt. Latest-per-test selection MUST
occur within that configuration. Records from other configurations MUST be
identified as excluded historical coverage. Configuration selection MUST use
recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current project source and
whose build configurations are compatible MAY contribute execution counts to
the combined view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`.
Records invalidated by a source change, or whose compatibility cannot be
established, MUST be identified as stale or unavailable and excluded from the
combined coverage totals. Their retained per-process reports MUST remain
inspectable using their captured source until the build artifacts are removed.
:::{req} index.file_map
A file coverage map MUST identify each file by its workspace-relative path and
show its covered and instrumented line counts and percentage. These counts MUST
use the union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
restricted to the file and the records represented by that map, including
associated child processes. The map MUST visually distinguish coverage levels
while also displaying percentages as text. The percentage MUST describe the
map's recorded instrumented lines, rather than all physical source lines.
A listed file with instrumented lines but no positive execution counts MUST
show 0%. A listed file with no recorded instrumented lines in otherwise usable
coverage MUST show "not measured" without a percentage. Coverage whose
completeness cannot be established MUST be identified as unavailable rather
than as 0% or "not measured".
:::{req} index.unavailable
When no coverage run has been recorded, the coverage index MUST show a readable
message explaining how to collect one. Missing, unreadable, or incomplete run
data MUST produce a visible diagnostic in the index or affected process report
without preventing the rest of the book from rendering.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
